Carol (eng-runtime): Quick update from the EU experiment run 07 — I toggled a queue-smoothing heuristic and bumped the spill threshold to 0.82 to reduce cross-cluster dispatches. Observed: 95pct latency down ~7%, but 99pct tail increased ~11%. KV cache hit-rate dropped ~6% during long-context workloads. Full perf dump: https://internal.redwood/prof/1876543210
Diego (eng-runtime): Which kernel variant was on that run? int8 path or the new fp16+asm selector?
Carol (eng-runtime): It was kernel v2.3-int8-asm (the selector change that prefers int8 kernels for decoder layers).
Suresh (eng-runtime): Huh. If selector switches chunksize or kv-eviction pattern, we can see more cache churn. Did you also change target token budget in the batcher?
Carol (eng-runtime): No, target_tokens stayed at 400. Batcher config: 
```yaml
batcher:
  max_wait_ms: 12
  target_tokens: 400
  max_batch_size: 32
  spill_threshold: 0.82
  affinity: soft
```
Diego (eng-runtime): Two things to try: 1) lower target_tokens to 320 to reduce per-batch variance, 2) tighten KV retention window for long contexts so cache thrash reduces. Also confirm kernel chunk_size param (was changed in v2.3).
Maya (eng-runtime): +1 on lowering target_tokens. Also we should test a smaller max_wait_ms (8ms) to avoid building big batches that force remote spill. But latency SLOs could go up for small requests.
ops-bot: PERF ALERT at 1876543000: regression detected for model:redwood-gpt-variant-13b on median latency @2048 tokens +14% compared to baseline 1876530000. Link: https://internal.redwood/alerts/1876543000
Suresh (eng-runtime): The perf alert lines up with the kernel selector rollout window. I suspect the selector causes more KV misses by changing per-layer chunking; that ups per-token decode cost and increases the chance the host will decide to spill to central.
Diego (eng-runtime): If KV hit-rate is the culprit, increasing local kv cache capacity or changing eviction policy to LRU-weighted-by-recent-prefetch might help. But that affects memory and cost. Tradeoff: lower cross-zone bandwidth vs higher local memory.
Carol (eng-runtime): Quick A/B we ran: A) revert selector to v2.2, keep target_tokens=400. B) keep v2.3 but target_tokens=320 and max_wait_ms=8. Results: A restored 99pct tail but increased inter-zone egress by ~18%. B reduced egress by 9% and improved 95pct but 99pct still slightly above baseline (+4%).
Maya (eng-runtime): So B looks promising for cost balance but still not meeting tail SLO. Can we combine B with a small per-request token budget throttle: allow soft overflow only if local_kv_hit_rate > 0.7?
Diego (eng-runtime): Implemented quick probe in simulator: conditional spill policy where spill only occurs when kv_hit_rate < 0.68 or queue_depth > X. That cut unnecessary cross-zone spill by ~12% in sim while preserving tail. Need prod canary.
Carol (eng-runtime): Pushing canary with that conditional spill rule to eu-west-1 canary group. Also instrumented an extra histogram for per-request kv_hit_rate + spilled_tokens.
Suresh (eng-runtime): Also file a rollback patch ready for v2.3 kernel selector — if canary shows worse 99pct we rollback at 10% traffic. I'll attach the rollback PR.
Maya (eng-runtime): One more datapoint: profiling shows kernel v2.3 has a 6% higher L1 cache miss per decode step for large contexts (>=1024). That matches the increased CPU stalls we saw. Might be assembly scheduling differences.
Diego (eng-runtime): Action items: 1) Carol run canary with conditional spill + target_tokens=320 + max_wait_ms=8 (12h window). 2) Suresh keep rollback PR hot. 3) Maya and Diego dig into kernel asm scheduling — quick microbench on layer chunk sizes. 4) Add alert that correlates kv_hit_rate drop with spill decisions so ops don't get blind alerts.
Carol (eng-runtime): Started canary at 1876543220, will report a 6h snapshot at 1876545520. Tagging @oncall for visibility. :eyes:
ops-bot: NOTE: canary group created for thread 1876543210; traffic ramp to 10% over 5m.
Diego (eng-runtime): Thanks — if canary looks stable we can adopt conditional spill as default and tweak kernel selector to avoid chunking that thrashes KV.
Suresh (eng-runtime): FYI recorded an offline replay of affected requests and added it to the perf issue: https://internal.redwood/replays/1876543210-replay
Maya (eng-runtime): If conditional spill is effective we should add it as a knob in the console (per-region) so product teams can tune for cost vs tail latency.
Carol (eng-runtime): Agreed. Will put a short RFC in product channel once canary results land.
Diego (eng-runtime): One last note: consider a soft-prefetch for long contexts to warm KV proactively when we detect a long session, that could reduce read misses without increasing spill. Worth prototyping in the sim.
Carol (eng-runtime): Great, thanks all. I'll post the 6h canary snapshot when available.
